notes.title: Goodbye Gutwhale!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

This post marks the end of work on Gutwhale! 
While you can find a more in depth post-mortem from my developer side here, this text is about the future of Gutwhale on Steam!

To make it short:

- Gutwhale will get no future updates on steam
- we have been unable to get achievements working
- the faulty control texts are fixed
- the savegame issues have been fixed
- we still do not know for sure why some controllers do not work

Steam does not automatically update your version of Gutwhale. If you want to get all the fixes & updates we have done, you need to reinstall the game.

We want to thank you all for your great feedback and suggestions. They are really appreciated and I truly wish I could have implemented some of them.

The short development time of Gutwhale created horrible code that is very hard to modify, as well as a pretty intense burnout/recovery period for me.
In addition to that, the steamworks plugins for the engine I used are no longer supported and we could not get complete steamworks integration running, meaning that we could not add steam achievements. This is probably also causing the controller issues, but we do not know.

I am very sorry that I could not give Gutwhale the support it needed as fast as you demanded it. I have learned my lesson and will give myself more time for future releases, so I do not need a month of recovery after release. I have also upgraded to the newest version of my engine, which should take care of all the Steamworks issues we had with Gutwhale.


Making Gutwhale in one month was an amazing experience. It was made way too fast and has problems that we can not fix because of that. We will give ourself more time to make the next game, both for our sake as well as for yours.

We all want to thank you for playing our game and hope that you enjoyed it.

Cheers,
Josh

notes.title: Two Weeks After Release - Quick Update
notes.content:
Heyo :)

It has been exactly 2 weeks since Gutwhale released!
Again, thank you all for your support, nice comments and helpful feedback!

Releasing a game is pretty stressful. After one exhausting month of development, I was not prepared for that. While my mental health and overall life is pretty good, I just felt frozen in place.

Not taking a few days off after release was a big mistake, and I have spend the last 2 weeks fiddling with small parts of the game, never making any real progress on the updates.

This post is just a quick apology for not being there fully to support the game, as well as to say that now, finally, I am able to work on updating Gutwhale.

Thanks for your patience,
josh

notes.title: Gutwhale - first update
notes.content:
Heyo :)

Tthe first update for Gutwhale has just been published!
I hope that steam will automatically update your game, but if you do not see a new loading screen when booting up the game, you have to quickly reinstall Gutwhale :/

This is just a small quality of life update, containing the following things:


 Savegame issue fixed
 Achievement room unlock issue fixed
 Restarting now resets combo, hat & score
 Added quick restart button (R on keyboard / Y on controller)
 Fixed wrong text on restarting with controller
 Added Dpad support to menu
 Added combosystem to nightmare mode


Now I will focus on the bigger tech tasks, such as getting Gutwhale to run reliably on Linux & Max, fixing the arcane controller problem & trying to get steam achievements and cloud save to work!

I am not a good coder, so some of these might not work out or may take some time!


For the new content we have been thinking hard and will probably expand the nightmare world to have its own hat unlock system and its own store as well as Bossfights!

Nothing set in stone there though :)

Thank you for you continued support and have a nice day!

Cheers,
josh

notes.title: The Future of Gutwhale! - Post Release Roadmap
notes.content:
Heyo!

Gutwhale has released and it has been amazing!
Thank you to everyone who played it, we are really happy that you seem to enjoy it and thank you so much for your 100% positive ratings :O

We have recieved a lot of feedback and after sifting through all of it, i am proud to present the roadmap for my continued work on Gutwhale!

First, I am going to polish the current version up:

- I am going to fix many of the little bugs and exploits that do not break the game but are a bit annoying.
- I am going to fix some small issues related to the games saving system
- I am going to rework the endgame content, so that it has more features for people who have beaten the complete game and are now competing for highscores and speedruns!


Then, I am going to attempt some backend coding things

- I will try my best to add steam achievements to Gutwhale
- I will research this one weird controller issue where new Xbox controllers do not get recognised by the game
- I will try to get Linux and Mac version running on Steam

Eventually, we will look into making new content for Gutwhale!

Some of you have beaten the game much, much faster than we anticipated and we want to add some hard challenges for you!

Right now I am thinkign about adding a Loop-System, where you can restart a run, but keep your score!
There might also be a way to create one infinitely long level, but I will have to look into that :)
And maybe we could add the bossfight that was cut for time back into Gutwhale?

If you have any suggestions for hard endgame content, please do not be shy and just tell us :)


While doing all of this, I will spend half of my time on marketing Gutwhale. I am going to go on some podcasts and streams and send a lot of emails!
We are also going to finally publish the development logs, as well as a video about how the game evolved visually!

If you have any questions, requests or want to report any bugs, please let us know on the discussion page!
And again, thank you all so much for playing our little game :))

cheers,
josh

notes.title: Gutwhale releases on April 6!!
notes.content:
Gutwhale release on April 6th!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37118717/17b51804588baab92f8328448dc679e6171089d5.png

We are all very excited and hope that you will love the game as much as we enjoyed making it :)

Gutwhale was made in one month, so some things that players normally expect from a game on steam are lacking, Here is what I will look into after the 6th:


 Linux & OS Builds (They are not stable rn. I will put them on Itch.io if you want to try)
 Steam Achievents 
 Cloud Saving


I will compile a more accurate Roadmap after release, when the first feedback from players has arrived :)

I never got to write those Devlogs, so I will also do that in the weeks after release!

Honestly, I am mostly nervous about the reception of Gutwhale these days and hope that all goes well :)

Stay safe and wash your hands,
josh

notes.title: Devlog #01 - The Beginning of Gutwhale
notes.content:
Hello!

My name is Josh and I am the designer, coder and producer of Gutwhale!
In this series of devlogs, I will talk about how Gutwhale became the game that it is now.

This series of posts will cover prototyping, design, production, implementation, trying to give good directions to my team as well as the whole process of getting a game on steam!

If there is something you are interested in, please do not be shy and just ask!
I can dedicate a couple of these posts to answering your questions about Gutwhale, or about game development in general!

But let us gets started:

The Beginning of Gutwhale


This game started as a little prototype I did for fun!
I coded someone with very long arms holding a gun, using Box2D physics:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37118717/194a0a2b9bad547e3ec4e98f3c25b006bad5e353.gif

I really enjoyed the feeling of this, but it was very hard and weird to control!
When you walked, the gun would lag behind you and it could get stuck on overhead ledges and stuff like that :)

But i liked the physicality of this prototype and continued in this direction, while trying to make it more accessible.

Here you can see the 2nd iteration:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37118717/5fee7e4033e672723c801131ebd47b66bb4b6808.gif

The gun is now firmly attached to the player, but still behaves like a physic object, trying to keep up with the players movement!
This enables players to shoot not only left or right, but at wide angles, if they time it right!

Compare to the first version, this was very easy to control. It lacked some of the physicality, but still felt pretty nice,
I made a modular gun holding system so playery could hold gun in different ways, to make it more interesting. Then I quickly added simple physics based enemies to shoot at:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37118717/46d820ea9469c85bc6873e0a0b2d36b324ede192.gif

I added a little bit of test art and it looked like this:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37118717/0f3602f9cfbba91e09addf772965d5d16198f2e7.gif

When I tried to make these enemies more interesting, i quickly realised something:

It is very, very hard to create reliable gameplay with physics. Often things spin out of control, enemies fly around and aiming a physics driven gun is really hard and feels bad when you are in intense situations!

So i decided to start from scratch and remove the physics, but keep the general "weighty" feeling of the game!

And this is how Gutwhale became a sidescrolling shooter!
It started as a fun thing that I then tried to make useable. That failed, but the core aspectets of these first prototypes remain in the game today!

Thanks for reading!
Next time I will talk about how the core mechanics of Gutwhale evolved over the span of a few, intense days of prototyping!

Cheers,
Josh
